name: flex
description: Typed flexbox container (direction/align/justify/wrap/gap) with FlexItem for per-child grow/shrink/basis controls.
designIntent: Layout utilities should be discoverable and tokenized: Flex turns display:flex into named props with token gaps, so spacing comes from the design system instead of scattered arbitrary classes. FlexItem handles per-child flex values through style (not runtime-built classes) so nothing gets purged from the stylesheet.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Allow items to wrap onto multiple lines.

props.name: as
props.description: Semantic element (FlexItem also supports 'li', Flex supports the structural elements).

props.name: grow
props.description: flex-grow for this FlexItem (true = 1, or a numeric string).

props.name: shrink
props.description: flex-shrink for this FlexItem (false = 0, or a numeric string).

examples.title: Toolbar row
examples.code:
<Flex align="center" justify="between" gap="sm">
  <Text size="sm" weight="medium">Title</Text>
  <Flex gap="sm">
    <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
    <Button size="sm">Save</Button>
  </Flex>
</Flex>
examples.description: Token gaps keep spacing on the design system grid.

examples.title: Sidebar + content
examples.description: FlexItem values render via inline style — arbitrary numeric utilities would be purged.

antiPatterns.title: Don't rebuild layout primitives with arbitrary classes
antiPatterns.explanation: Runtime-built class strings (grow-[${value}]) never make it into the compiled CSS. Use Flex/FlexItem props — they emit style values where Tailwind can't.
antiPatterns.example:
<div className={`grow-[${n}]`}>  // purged at build
<FlexItem grow={n}>  // works

antiPatterns.title: Don't wrap a single child
antiPatterns.explanation: A Flex with one child adds a pointless layout layer — use Block with utilities instead.

accessibility.implementation: Renders div/span/section… — no interactive or live behavior is added
accessibility.userRequirements: Interactive children keep their own keyboard/ARIA contracts

accessibility.implementation: flex-wrap reflows visually; DOM order (reading order) never changes
accessibility.userRequirements: Put items in logical reading order regardless of visual layout

compositionRules.relationship: Flex for one-axis alignment; Grid for two-axis layout
Blocks are the semantic wrappers Flex arranges
